dateline: Hawthorne, CA / Boca Chica, TX — May 2002–Present
heroHeadline: Aug 21: SpaceX Flies Second Double-Header of the Month — Starlink 15-20 & 10-39 Push Constellation Past 11,000
heroSubtitle: 8,874 days since SpaceX founding — SpaceX launched two more Falcon 9 Starlink missions on Aug 21: Starlink 15-20 from Vandenberg (B1100, 9th flight, 29 satellites) and Starlink 10-39 from Cape Canaveral (B1078, 30th flight — the 6th booster ever to reach that mark, after an Aug 20 scrub), pushing the Starlink constellation to roughly 11,000 satellites in orbit and SpaceX past its 99th-100th Falcon-family launch of 2026 (reports vary on the exact tally). SPCX shares closed at $136.97 on Aug 22, up 2.2% from Aug 21's $134.00, clawing back some of the prior week's slide that followed a second post-IPO lock-up tranche (~319M shares) unlocking Aug 20. That volatility followed the Aug 17-18 window, when mid-August Form 13F filings revealed SpaceX's largest institutional shareholders for the first time since its June IPO — Alphabet, Fidelity, Gigafund, Saudi Arabia's PIF, and Nvidia (via its xAI stake) — sending SPCX up 4.45% on Aug 17 before a growth-stock selloff pulled it back. On the Starship side, Ship 41 completed single- and six-engine static fires at Starbase on Aug 19 toward IFT-14, while Booster 21 remains in Mega Bay 1 awaiting its own static fire; the flight's NET target has reportedly slipped from late August toward early-to-mid September.
